tasks.desc: Implement brute-force verifier, baseline open-arc DP, inclusion-exclusion DP, and CDQ/NTT solver.
Run self-test and medium random stress tests (N up to 20) comparing all solvers; fix any mismatches in CDQ/NTT or DP.
Handle edge cases (N=1, first vertex must be B, last vertex must be W, automatic N! when R[t]<t).
Force DIRECT_M small and stress-test solve_large against solve_direct on random and structured N=3000-10000 cases with active m>2000; fix any correctness mismatches.
Run timed N=200000 benchmarks for alternating, long-run, and random strings; fix performance bottlenecks.
Finalize solver selection, remove fallbacks/debug code, and ensure final program reads stdin and writes stdout.

proposals: Implement and test the inclusion-exclusion DP over bad black-prefix cuts, with early zero checks, and first validate it by brute force for small N.

Try to evaluate the DP using divide-and-conquer with NTT, but carefully bound convolution lengths and consider grouping equal C_t values; in many strings only the first occurrence of each C_t can contribute.

Investigate whether the worst-case alternating pattern can be handled by a faster formal-power-series inversion for the factorial-kernel recurrence, and whether other patterns can be decomposed into simpler segments.
Explore the inverse-permutation prefix-maximum formulation and see if it leads to a determinant, rook-polynomial, or ballot/reflection formula that avoids online convolution.

Explore the open-arc sweep DP and possible run-length or generating-function optimizations, especially for long runs of the same color, while keeping the boundary condition at nonnegative balance in mind.
